summary: Tolterodine is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist for overactive bladder with urge incontinence, urgency and frequency. Extended-release 4 mg once daily is the usual dose, reduced to 2 mg in mild-moderate hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, or with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation) and rare QT prolongation are key concerns; contraindicated in urinary or gastric retention and uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma.
indications: Treatment of overactive bladder with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency and frequency

dosage.n: May lower to 2 mg based on response/tolerability

dosage.d: 2 mg twice daily; may lower to 1 mg twice daily
2 mg once daily (ER) or 1 mg twice daily (IR)
dosage.n: Avoid ER if CCr <10 mL/min or Child-Pugh C

admin: Take extended-release capsule orally once daily with water and swallow whole; do not crush or chew
May be taken with or without food (no food effect on ER)
Reduce to 2 mg ER daily in mild-moderate hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, or with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors
Do not use ER capsules if CCr <10 mL/min or in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C)
Advise caution with driving/machinery until CNS effects are known
moa: Tolterodine is a competitive antagonist of acetylcholine at postganglionic muscarinic receptors. Blockade of bladder muscarinic receptors reduces detrusor contraction, increasing bladder capacity and reducing urgency/frequency. It is metabolized by the liver (CYP2D6) to the active 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine (5-HMT), which contributes significantly to the antimuscarinic effect; both show high muscarinic specificity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to tolterodine, its ingredients, or fesoterodine (shared 5-HMT metabolite)
relative: GI obstructive disorders or decreased GI motility
Known QT prolongation or class IA/III antiarrhythmic use
monitor: Signs of urinary or gastric retention

preg: There are no human data to inform drug-associated risk. Animal studies showed embryo-lethality and fetal abnormalities only at exposures well above clinical. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether tolterodine is excreted in human milk; it is excreted in mouse milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended during therapy; consider the drug's importance to the mother.
renal: For severe renal impairment (CCr 10-30 mL/min), recommended ER dose is 2 mg once daily. Not recommended in patients with CCr <10 mL/min.
hepatic: For mild to moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B), recommended ER dose is 2 mg once daily. Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C).

major: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) - increase exposure; reduce dose to 2 mg ER daily
Class IA (quinidine, procainamide) / Class III (sotalol, amiodarone) antiarrhythmics and other QT-prolonging drugs - additive QT risk
moderate: Other anticholinergic/antimuscarinic agents - increased dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, retention
Potent CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine) - increase tolterodine but no dose adjustment needed (active moiety little changed)
interactions.food: No clinically significant effect of food on extended-release pharmacokinetics.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; may add to drowsiness and dizziness.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause modest QT-interval prolongation on ECG.

monitoring: Symptoms of urinary retention, especially with bladder outflow obstruction
Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, confusion)
QT interval in patients with risk factors or on QT-prolonging drugs
Bowel function in patients with GI motility disorders
counsel: Swallow the extended-release capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew
Expect dry mouth and constipation; use sugar-free gum/fluids and fiber as needed
Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you (may cause drowsiness/blurred vision)
Avoid alcohol; report difficulty urinating, severe constipation, or facial/throat swelling
Take once daily at about the same time each day
pk: ER serum peak 2-6 hours after dose
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light
pearls: Reduce ER to 2 mg daily with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, severe renal impairment (CCr 10-30), or mild-moderate hepatic impairment
Active metabolite 5-HMT is shared with fesoterodine - cross-hypersensitivity applies
Use caution / consider ECG in patients with congenital long QT or on class IA/III antiarrhythmics
Anticholinergic burden matters in the elderly (confusion, falls); avoid stacking antimuscarinics
ER 4 mg daily is bioequivalent in active moiety to IR 2 mg twice daily
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose can cause severe central anticholinergic effects. Treat with supportive care and gastric decontamination (activated charcoal); ECG monitoring is recommended because of QT-prolongation potential. Manage anticholinergic toxicity symptomatically.
